newsitem.title: FRANCE: French senate chair says euro needs 8-10 members.
newsitem.headline: French senate chair says euro needs 8-10 members.

text.p: Reney Monory, chairman of the French senate, said in a radio interview that the euro needed at least eight to 10 member countries at the start.
Monory said that the early election was needed to better prepare the euro, due in 1999.

"If we would have waited until 1998 (the original election date), we would have been in a weaker position compared to our partners... There have to be at least eight or 10 at the start," he told Europe 1 radio.
He also urged France to be a little more liberal in general economic policies.
He said that now that the deficits of the past had been cut there was a place for a new economic policy and he said France needed a more liberal economic approach.

"We will not have in France a U.S. style liberalism ... but we will certainly have a more pronounced liberalism. You do not have to make excuses for being liberal. It's the only way to create wealth," Monory said.
Asked to comment on a poll finding that 68 percent of French people fear increased austerity measures after the election, Monory said he did not believe that would be the case.
"That is not possible because we do not want to have a policy of additional austerity. On the contrary... we will reduce taxes, we will let social charges come down," Monory said.
